description: §19.7.1 / §18.6 (S474) — on a failable result `else` covers the success value only. Here every error variant (`.Locked`, `.Denied`) has its own arm, so the trailing `else` takes only the success value: the match is accepted, a wrong password yields "denied" and the right one "LOGGED IN". The accepted near-miss of E-MATCH-ELSE-ABSORBS-ERROR.
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S474 "⭐ RULED — `else` on a failable match; `scrml fix` S466 readings" item 1 — "on a failable subject, `else` covers success variants only. Errors need an explicit arm, `_ e`, or `!{}`"
rationale: §19.7.1 (S474): in a `match` on a failable result, a plain `_` / `else` arm covers the success value `.Ok` only. Explicit error arms followed by `else` are therefore exhaustive and absorb no error, so no E-MATCH-ELSE-ABSORBS-ERROR and no E-TYPE-020; at run time a failure runs its own arm, never the `else`.
